purpose: Nizatidine is used to treat heartburn, acid reflux, and conditions where your stomach makes too much acid, like ulcers. It can help heal ulcers in your stomach or the upper part of your small intestine. It also helps relieve the burning discomfort caused by stomach acid backing up into your esophagus.
how_it_works: Your stomach has tiny receptors that respond to a chemical called histamine, which tells your stomach to make acid. Nizatidine blocks those receptors so your stomach produces less acid. With less acid, your stomach and esophagus have a chance to heal and you feel less discomfort.
common_side_effects: Most people tolerate this medication well. Some people may experience headache, dizziness, diarrhea, constipation, or an upset stomach. You might also notice mild tiredness or a runny nose.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Avoid taking it with alcohol, which can worsen stomach irritation. If you experience chest pain, difficulty swallowing, unexplained weight loss, or vomiting blood, contact your doctor right away as these could be signs of something more serious. Let your doctor know all other medications you are taking, as nizatidine can interact with some drugs.
typical_dosing: For heartburn or acid reflux, a common dose is 75 mg taken as needed, up to twice a day. For ulcers or prescription use, the typical dose is 150 mg twice daily or 300 mg once at bedtime. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's specific instructions for your situation.
